clue.text: Opening consulting room with minimal intrusion

blocks.note: a small opening in a door, made for a key
in Britain a doctor's consulting room is called a surgery

explanation.surface: A doctor discreetly opens up a consulting room without disturbing anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a surgery is also the room where a GP sees patients, which lets the two halves read as a door and a room.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical technique operates through tiny incisions, so the patient's body suffers only very slight invasion.

clue.text: Warm wine for the family

blocks.note: red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: Mulled wine is served to the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives, the people related by blood, which is one's family.

clue.text: Child from New Street touching the Queen

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A child from New Street meets the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: New Street looks like a place name, but the words are taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, so it stands for a child.

clue.text: Start to break up a stone

indicators.note: breaking something up scatters its parts, so the following word's letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone begins to smash a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, so it means the start.

clue.text: One gets ulcers put right for a pound

indicators.note: putting something right means rearranging it into proper order, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone has their ulcers cured for the price of a single pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound looks like money, but it is a pen where stray animals are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is a fenced pen for stray animals, which is a kind of fenced area.

clue.text: See 1
Must I drop from the stairs to see them?

indicators.note: dropping something from a word means taking that letter out of it

explanation.surface: Must I fall down the stairs to see stars?
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: a nasty fall downstairs makes you 'see stars'. Remove I from STAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to what a dazed person proverbially sees after a bang on the head: twinkling lights in the sky.

clue.text: Sends back statements about former spouse

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Accounts are given about someone's former husband or wife.
explanation.walkthrough: About here wraps round rather than meaning 'concerning'; the former spouse lands just after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-export goods is to ship imported goods out again, sending them back abroad.

clue.text: Senior to exhibit part of red letter upside down

indicators.note: exhibiting part of the phrase means the letters sit inside it, displayed
in a down clue, upside down means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: read backwards, these words show the run inside them

explanation.surface: An older person displays part of a letter turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is an older person, and as an adjective elder means senior in age.

clue.text: Americans travelling in southeast Kenya

indicators.note: things that are travelling move about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: American tourists on safari in southeast Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name, especially outside the US, for people from the United States.

clue.text: There's a hole in sister's things

definitions.note: loosely: these are words naming things

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other

blocks.note: a nun is a sister; the possessive drops its apostrophe
the letter O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: A nun's belongings have a hole in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Sister is a religious title for a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, nouns are the words that name people, places and objects, so they stand loosely for things.

clue.text: Type of claret not finished, having no date attached

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: N is a short form of no
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A bottle of claret, unfinished, with no vintage date on its label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of claret' looks like a wine description, but Type alone is the definition: printers' type.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarendon is a bold typeface used by printers, so it is a type in the typographic sense.

clue.text: Fair Susan holding love back, being virtuous

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece goes inside the name
back means the resulting group of letters is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Fair-haired Susan holds back her love, being a good person.
explanation.walkthrough: Back applies after the love is tucked inside the name, so the whole short group is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous describes someone morally upright, which is the same as virtuous.

clue.text: It takes a second to split up honest funds

indicators.note: splitting a word up means something is pushed in between its letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: It takes only a moment to divide up honestly earned money.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is the money available to someone or an organisation, their resources or funds.

clue.text: The wife's language!

blocks.note: first meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old ...' is a man's wife, from 'Duchess of Fife'
second meaning: the tongue spoken in the Netherlands

explanation.surface: A man remarks on which tongue his wife speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two meanings; 'my old Dutch' is London rhyming slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses this word for a wife, and it also names the national tongue of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Bound to need whisky for the game

blocks.note: to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to need a whisky to play the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to need' reads as 'certain to need', but Bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Type of service is shortly to be prepared for war

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its opening letter

blocks.note: an underarm serve, hit from below shoulder level

explanation.surface: A style of serving is about to be readied for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose the I from IS to leave S.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who are under arms are equipped with weapons and ready to fight.

clue.text: Bad-tempered Syd held up savings scheme on credit nearly

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted so the name reads from bottom to top
nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a British tax-free savings scheme
buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: Grumpy Syd is delayed by a savings plan bought nearly on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: PEP, a Personal Equity Plan, was a British tax-free investment from 1987 to 1999; 'on tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspeptic literally means suffering indigestion, and by extension irritable and grumpy.

clue.text: Forgiveness concerning a self-imposed duty

blocks.note: a mission is a task one sets oneself

explanation.surface: Pardon is sought regarding an obligation someone took on.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission of sins is their pardoning, so the word is a formal synonym for forgiveness.

clue.text: Type of dress with belt getting smaller

explanation.surface: A frock with a belt that keeps shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless dress has no shoulder straps, so the word describes a style of gown.

clue.text: Bad bet shatters Harry, which is a disappointment

indicators.note: something bad is wrongly formed, so the letters of the next word are muddled
shattering something means breaking into it, so one piece lodges inside the other

blocks.note: to harry or sack a town is to plunder it

explanation.surface: A losing wager devastates poor Harry, a real letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a man's name; here it is the verb meaning to pillage.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse in progress, and so something that brings disappointment.

clue.text: Assess university in depression

indicators.note: in places one element within the other

blocks.note: a sump is a pit or hollow where liquid collects
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student at university is feeling low and being judged.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum someone up is to form an overall judgement of them, to size them up.

clue.text: A sweet cleaner put up with worry

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means raised so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a mop is a cleaning tool

explanation.surface: A kind cleaning lady tolerated anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweet cleaner reads as a nice charlady, and put up with as tolerated. A Pomfret cake is a small round liquorice sweet from Pontefract in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomfret cakes are small black liquorice confections, so the word names a sweet.

clue.text: Subject to pretty intensive cross-examination initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

blocks.note: the leading letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone is subjected to a fierce grilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as one phrase, but Subject alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a matter under discussion, the theme or subject of a talk.

clue.text: Cat or dog, say, needs it to be small in Montpellier, say

explanation.surface: A pet animal needs to be little in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Montpellier is a city in southern France, so the definition asks for the French word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is the French adjective for little, as spoken in a French city.

clue.text: Unusually, men go cash for this dress

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters come in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Strangely, the men head out to spend money on a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar and slit skirt.

clue.text: Child has a tea-maker, but where might the milk be?

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for child
a tea urn is a large vessel for making tea

explanation.surface: A child has the tea urn ready, but where is the milk?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks a tea-time question, yet it defines the dairy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is held in a churn, a large metal can or a vessel for making butter.

clue.text: Not applicable to Geldorf, who's a wealthy person

blocks.note: N/A is the abbreviation for not applicable
Bob Geldof, the Irish singer who organised Live Aid

explanation.surface: Something doesn't apply to the rock star Geldof, a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Geldof, misspelt Geldorf in the clue, is the Irish musician behind Live Aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob, originally a Mughal governor, came to mean any very rich man, especially one enriched in India.

clue.text: Start unit that's different for opposing monopolies

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Launch a new department set up to fight big business cartels.
explanation.walkthrough: Start looks like the instruction; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitrust laws, chiefly American, are designed to break up cartels and prevent single firms dominating markets.

clue.text: Pipe obtained from branch that is by river

blocks.note: BR is an abbreviation for branch
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A pipe is carved from a riverside branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Briar pipes are carved from the root of a heath shrub, so the surface's branch is a plausible but false source.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier, or briar, is a tobacco pipe made from the woody root of the tree heath.

clue.text: Influential group using cookhouse cupboard

explanation.surface: Powerful insiders meet using a cupboard in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cabinet is a leader's informal circle of trusted advisers who wield power behind the scenes.

clue.text: See 27
